title: Split any feature exceeding 2 new tables, 2 async jobs, or 2 integrations

facts.note: Task text names feature planning, scoping, or the limited resource kinds.
Planner artifacts that declare a feature's scope.
The rule applies in any phase; a phase observer only helps route an over-limit feature found during implementation or review back to the planner. It is not an exclusion.
Counting from plan prose needs judgement. Only tables are qualified by 'new'; async jobs and integrations count whether they are new or existing. A structured counter would be a new observer.

fires: A planned feature introduces 3 new tables.
A feature uses 3 async jobs, even if some of them already exist.
A feature depends on 3 integrations, even if some of them are already wired up.
During implementation or review, a feature turns out to exceed one of the ceilings.
doesNotFire: A feature with exactly 2 new tables, 2 async jobs, and 2 integrations (the limit is not exceeded).
A feature that touches more than 2 existing tables but adds at most 2 new ones, and stays within the job and integration ceilings.

given: A feature whose scope includes tables, async jobs, or integrations
when: The planner authors, revises, or reviews the feature, or finds during any phase that the feature is over-limit
then: If the feature has more than 2 new tables, more than 2 async jobs, or more than 2 integrations, split it so that every resulting feature stays within all three limits.
prefer: Split along the excess. Move the extra tables, jobs, or integrations into a separate feature with its own acceptance.
avoid: Leaving a feature that exceeds any one limit unsplit, or treating the limits as advisory.
Gaming the count, e.g. merging distinct jobs or tables into one, or wrapping several dependencies behind one facade.
Excluding existing jobs or integrations from the count. Only tables are limited to new ones.
why: Tables bring maintenance, schema-evolution, and performance cost. Async jobs bring operational complexity (monitoring, retry, inconsistency). Integrations bring external dependencies, security exposure, and failures you cannot control.
evidence: For every feature, the reviewer counts new tables, async jobs, and integrations and confirms each count is <= 2.
If the original scope exceeded any limit, the plan shows the split into features that each satisfy all three limits.
verifier_detail: Hard limits (term hard_limit: per-feature ceilings that force a split): new_tables = 2, async_jobs = 2, integrations = 2. The comparison is inclusive: <= 2 passes, > 2 requires a split.
Each limit is checked independently. Exceeding any one is a violation, even when the other two are within bounds.

Rationale per limit, from the source: new_tables (high maintenance/schema-evolution/perf cost); async_jobs (operational complexity: monitoring, retry, inconsistency); integrations (external deps, security, uncontrolled failure).
Only 'tables' carries the 'new' qualifier in the source. async_jobs and integrations have no new-only qualifier, so count every one the feature uses. The source has no phase restriction.
